papers.title: Logics vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between doctrines, encoding 2-categories of theories in predicate logic, and fragments of geometric logic, defined through Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi. After a brief historical account of the notion of doctrine, we propose our working definition. Our main result then establishes a Galois connection between doctrines and subgeometric logics. This connection suggests a mirror symmetry between the world of doctrines and the world of logics, in which constructions and results on either side admit counterparts on the other. We develop this symmetry through constructions of syntactic categories and classifying topoi in both settings, recovering the familiar examples from categorical logic. We prove paired Diaconescu-type theorems and give symmetric universal characterisations of the two closure operators induced by the Galois connection. Finally, we show that passing from a doctrine to its closure induces a reflection between the corresponding 2-categories of algebras, and we relate this reflection to conceptual completeness.

papers.title: Analytification and tropicalization via hyperfields and definable types
papers.abstract: We study the analytification and tropicalization of algebraic varieties over valued fields via Jun's spaces of hyperfield points. Our main new objects are a family of power-tropical hyperfields $H_n$ and their inverse limit $H$, recording at each level the class of a leading term modulo $n$-th powers of the residue field. They yield an enhanced tropicalization of the associated space $X(H)$, strictly finer than the Berkovich one exactly when the multiplicative group of the residue field is non-divisible: it specialises to the Berkovich analytification when the residue field is algebraically closed, to the real analytification of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu when it is real closed, and to a new $p$-adic analytification when it is $p$-adically closed. Over henselian valued fields of equicharacteristic $0$ we then construct a model-theoretic avatar of $X(H)$: the space $\widehat{X}_T$ of definable types orthogonal to the value group, which sharpens the geometry in the spirit of Hrushovski and Loeser and recovers their space over algebraically closed valued fields. We show that $\widehat{X}_T$ is strictly pro-definable, satisfies a model-theoretic Payne theorem, and definable compactness in such spaces satisfies a Heine-Borel type characterization. As an application, we analytify $p$-adic semi-algebraic sets and prove a strong density theorem for their tropicalizations, the exact $p$-adic counterpart of the real one of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu.

papers.title: Searching for the power rangers
papers.abstract: We develop a method for studying centralizers of generic elements in some large Polish groups. We identify a condition which enables us to show that the range of each power map is comeager; a strengthening of this condition allows us to prove that a generic element embeds in a flow (a continuous, one-parameter subgroup). This approach enables us to answer the question that motivated this work : we prove that a generic isometry of the Urysohn space (or the Urysohn sphere) embeds in a flow. We also obtain information on the centralizer of a generic isometry; we show that it contains an infinite-dimensional torus and that torsion elements are dense in it. To illustrate the flexibility of our method, we apply it to two other Polish groups. The first is the group of measure-preserving automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we recover results of King and of de la Rue and de Sam Lazaro. Finally we apply our technique to the group of nonsingular automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we deduce that a generic nonsingular automorphism embeds in a flow, answering a question of Danilenko and Silva.

papers.title: Properties of theories whose algebras are free
papers.abstract: A hard theorem of Givant classifies the finitary algebraic theories for which every algebra is free. From it, one easily deduces that all such theories are minimal (adding any further equations makes them trivial) and have a well-defined notion of dimension (free algebras on sets of different cardinality are never isomorphic). We prove both these properties directly, without the aid of Givant's theorem.

papers.title: Computable presentations of separable Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: For every right-c.e.\ real $p\in(1,2)$, $L^p[0,1]$ has a computable presentation. The proof combines an effective stability modulus for almost isometric embeddings with a Fra\"{\i}ss\'e-style construction in which the exponent varies. In the same range, if $\ell^p$ has a computable presentation, then $p$ is computable. Combining these with the known results gives the computable presentability classification for all separable Lebesgue spaces. We also formulate an effective Fra\"{\i}ss\'e theorem for Banach spaces and apply it to obtain a computable presentation of the Gurarij Banach space.

papers.title: The Cofinality of Generating Familes
papers.abstract: The topology of a separable metrizable space $M$ is \emph{generated} by a family $\mathcal{C}$ of its subsets provided that a set $A\subseteq M$ is closed in $M$ if and only if $A\cap C$ is closed in $C$ for each $C\in \mathcal{C}$. The \emph{sequentiality number}, $\mathop{seq}(M)$, and \emph{$k$-ness number}, $\mathop{k}(M)$, of $M$, are the minimum size of a generating family of convergent sequences, respectively compact subsets. Let $\mathfrak{b}$ be the minimum size of an unbounded set in $\omega^\omega$ with the mod finite order. For a cardinal $\kappa$, the \emph{covering number}, $\mathop{cov}(\kappa)$, is the minimum size of a family of countable subsets of $\kappa$ so that every countable subset of $\kappa$ is contained in an element of the family. It is shown using the Tukey order on relations that (1) $\mathop{seq}(M)=\mathop{cov}(|M|)\cdot \mathfrak{b}$, unless $M$ is locally small (every point of $M$ has a neighborhood of size strictly less than $|M|$) in which case $\mathop{seq}(M)=\lim_{\mu <|M|} \mathop{cov}(\mu)\cdot \mathfrak{b}$ and (2) $k(M)$ is in the interval $[kc(M)\cdot\mathfrak{b},\mathop{cov}(kc(M))\cdot \mathfrak{b}]$, where $kc(M)$ is the minimum number of compact sets that cover $M$. Solutions to problems of van Douwen's on the $k$-ness number of analytic and of co-analytic spaces are deduced.

papers.title: The Game-Theoretic Kat\v{e}tov Order and Idealised Effective Subtoposes
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the longstanding problem of determining the structure of the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order in the Effective Topos, known to effectively embed the Turing degrees. In a surprising discovery, we show that the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order is in fact tightly controlled by the combinatorics of filters on $\omega$, raising deep questions about how combinatorial and computable complexity interact, both within this order and beyond it. To make the connection precise, we introduce a game-theoretic (''gamified'') variant of the Kat\v{e}tov order on filters over $\omega$, which turns out to exhibit a striking mix of coarseness and subtlety. For one, it is strictly coarser than the classical Rudin-Keisler order and, when viewed dually on ideals, collapses all MAD families to a single equivalence class. On the other hand, the order also supports a rich internal structure, including an infinite strictly ascending chain of ideal classes, which we identify by way of a new separation technique. From the computability-theoretic perspective, we show that a computable (and extended) variant of the gamified Kat\v{e}tov order is isomorphic to the original $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order. Moreover, our work brings into focus a new degree-spectrum invariant for filters $\mathcal{F}$, $$\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F}):=\{\,[f\colon\omega\to\omega] \mid f\leq_{\mathrm{LT}} \mathcal{F} \},$$ which is shown to always determine a proper initial segment of the Turing degrees. Extending this, given any non-principal $\Delta^1_1$ filter $\mathcal{F}$, we show that $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F})$ is precisely the class of hyperarithmetic degrees. This significantly generalises previous results obtained by van Oosten \cite{vO14} and Kihara \cite{Kih23}. The proofs draw on ideas from general topology, descriptive set theory, and computability theory.

papers.title: Reflections on Trusting Lean
papers.abstract: It is known, by works of Werner and Carneiro, that the type theory of Lean (and indeed of CIC plus a version of choice) is equiconsistent with ZFC plus "there are infinitely many strongly inaccessible cardinals". We prove a finer connection between these two formal systems; namely, given any formula in the language of second order arithmetic, that formula is provable in the aforementioned extension of ZFC if and only if the same formula, when viewed as a type in Lean, is inhabited.

papers.title: A Study in Solution Models for SAT using the PBNF-transform
papers.abstract: In this article, we use the PBNF-transform, or Polynomial Boolean Normal Form, described earlier in two articles and now extended to higher arity, to solve Boolean satisfiability problems (SAT), which are part of the P versus NP problem. SAT consists of a statement of conjunctions of clauses, and in our SAT-solving models, we dualize the logical equations, inverting the problem by \emph{multiplying} letters (literals) in the transferred clauses, now phrases: $pqrs\cdots s_{\ell}$, and using a binary iterated composition based on \emph{adding polynomials} for the conjunctions in our solution formula. We obtain Polynomial Boolean Equations, PBE=0, by also renaming the truth value $1\mapsto 0$(T). To find a solution, we look for repeating literals in the clauses to factor out. With reversed literal repetition, we can even reduce the CNF to the sum of the transformed clauses.

papers.title: Non-aware computable presentations of randomizations
papers.abstract: Let 2 be the two-element structure in the empty signature. We build a computable presentation Q of the Borel randomization $2^{[0,1)}$ in which neither constant random variable is a computable point. Consequently, Q is not aware. This gives a negative answer to a question of Cuervo Ovalle and Goldbring \cite{CG}. We also construct a countable structure $M$ with no computable presentation but $M^{[0,1)}$ has a computable presentation. This answers another question and establishes the necessity of the awareness condition stated in one of the main theorems in \cite{CG}.

papers.title: Set-theoretic inevitability
papers.abstract: After defining the concept of inevitability for statements with the modal logic of forcing, we raise the question of which statements are inevitable under $\mathsf{ZFC}$ and under large cardinal hypotheses. We show that $\mathsf{SOA}$ (defined as $\mathsf{ZFC}^-$ + $\mathsf V=\mathsf{HC}$) plus the $\boldsymbol\Sigma^1_2$-perfect set property is $\mathsf{ZFC}$-inevitable, and that Projective Determinacy is inevitable in the theory of $\mathsf{ZFC}$ with a proper class of Woodin cardinals. We then discuss the possible conceptual significance of these results for the foundations of set theory.

papers.title: There is no universal $F_\sigma$ equivalence relation
papers.abstract: Rosendal proved that any $K_\sigma$ equivalence relation is Borel reducible to $\ell_\infty$. We prove that for every $F_\sigma$ equivalence relation $F$ on a Polish space, there is an $F_\sigma$ real linear subspace $H$ of $\ell_2$ such that the coset relation $x\mathrel{E_H}y$ if and only if $x-y\in H$ has no Baire-measurable reduction to $F$. In particular, there is no $F_\sigma$ equivalence relation universal under Borel reducibility for all $F_\sigma$ equivalence relations. This answers a question of Rosendal.

papers.title: Groups satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers are complete co-analytic
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the set of groups satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is a complete co-analytic subset of the Polish space of countable groups. This answers a question of Wesolek and Williams.

papers.title: A declarative approach to specifying Paxos using three-valued modal fixpoint logic
papers.abstract: We present Three-valued Fixpoint Quorum Logic, or 3muQL for short; a three-valued modal fixed-point logic designed for declaratively specifying and reasoning about distributed algorithms, such as the Paxos consensus algorithm. Our methodology represents a distributed algorithm as a logical theory, enabling correctness properties to be derived directly within the framework -- or revealing logical errors in the algorithm's design when they exist. 3muQL adopts a declarative approach, specifying the overall logic of computation without prescribing control flow. Notably, message-passing and state-transitions are not explicitly modelled, and notions of 'quorum' are abstracted from concrete thresholds to abstract modal operators. This distinguishes our framework from approaches like TLA+. The logical abstraction emphasises the essence of distributed algorithms, offering a novel perspective on their specification and reasoning. We define the syntax and semantics of 3muQL, explore its theoretical properties, and demonstrate its applicability through a detailed treatment of the Paxos consensus algorithm. By presenting Paxos as a logical theory and deriving its standard correctness properties, we showcase the framework's capacity to handle non-trivial distributed systems. We envision 3muQL as a versatile tool for specifying and reasoning about distributed algorithms. The Paxos example highlights the framework's ability to capture intricate details, offering a new lens through which distributed algorithms can be specified, studied, and checked. The ideas we present are easily implemented, and to demonstrate this we have implemented a freely-available proof-of- concept 3muQL model-checker, as an effective prototyping tool.

papers.title: Cut elimination for the alternation-free modal mu-calculus
papers.abstract: We present a syntactic cut-elimination procedure for the alternation-free fragment of the modal mu-calculus. Cut reduction is carried out within a cyclic proof system, where proofs are finitely branching but may be non-wellfounded. The structure of such proofs is exploited to directly transform a cyclic proof with cuts into a cut-free one, without detouring through other logics or relying on intermediate machinery for regularisation. Novel ingredients include the use of multicuts and results from the theory of well-quasi-orders, the later used in the termination argument.

papers.title: Star operation, microscopic sets and porous sets
papers.abstract: This paper explores the interplay between star operations, microscopic sets, and porous sets. The study focuses on the Galvin-Mycielski-Solovay theorem, which characterizes strongly measure zero sets and their interactions with meager sets. Results include the investigation of the star operation $\mathcal{F}^*$ and its properties. The paper also examines the relationship between porous sets and microscopic sets. Additionally, the work presents constructions of families $\mathcal{F}$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Z}), \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Z}^\omega),$ and $\mathcal{P}(2^\omega)$ that satisfy $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}^*$. Theorems and lemmas are provided to establish conditions under which $\mathcal{F}^{**} = \mathcal{F}$ and to analyze the implications of the Borel Conjecture and its dual. The paper concludes with a discussion of microscopic sets and their properties, including their interactions with porous sets and the non-equivalence of certain classes of sets.

papers.title: Approximation of structures:local and global
papers.abstract: We provide a mathematically rigorous definition of local approximation and demonstrate its applicability to some interesting classes of structures. In particular, we prove that any compact simple Lie group is locally approximated by finite groups. The definition and main examples are motivated by physics but the techniques are of model theory. Namely, we introduce the ultraproduct of emerging metric structures, which generalises the ultraproduct in metric model theory.

papers.title: The Limits of Arithmetical Pluralism: Incompleteness, Large Cardinals, and Graded Non-Pluralism
papers.abstract: G\"odelian incompleteness yields arithmetical sentences \(A\) such that \(\mathsf{PA}+A\) and \(\mathsf{PA}+\neg A\) are both consistent. Are such extensions equally legitimate? I propose graded epistemic arithmetical non-pluralism: justification for choosing between them varies with the set-theoretic strength of \(A\). I defend \(\mathsf{PA}+\mathsf{Con}(\mathsf{PA})\) and show that Friedman's concrete incompleteness results pose a serious challenge to non-pluralism about first-order arithmetic. Resolving the selection problem for such sentences turns on justifying large cardinals. Defending graded non-pluralism thus engages G\"odel's programme and the justification of very large cardinals.

papers.title: Coanalytic subfields and bases of prescribed dimension
papers.abstract: Assuming $V=L$, we construct proper coanalytic subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ and coanalytic Hamel and transcendence bases of every possible Hausdorff dimension, uniformly in the relevant parameters. There is a single lightface $\Pi^1_1$ set $G\subseteq[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ whose sections $A_\alpha$ are proper subfields with $\dim_{\mathrm H}A_\alpha=\alpha$, form a strictly increasing chain, and satisfy $A_\alpha=\bigcup_{\beta<\alpha}A_\beta$ for $\alpha>0$. For every $n\ge1$, every countable subfield $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ and every $s\in[0,n]$, we construct a coanalytic Hamel basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$ over $K$ of Hausdorff dimension $s$. Likewise, for every countable subfield $K\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ and every $s\in[0,2]$, we construct a coanalytic transcendence basis of $\mathbb{C}$ over $K$ of Hausdorff dimension $s$. In each case, the bases are sections of a single lightface $\Pi^1_1$ relation, uniformly in codes for the coefficient field and in the prescribed dimension, as well as in $n$ for Hamel bases. More generally, we prove a uniform theorem for suitably coded families of pregeometries on Euclidean spaces. The constructions combine Cantor sets of controlled dimension with hyperarithmetic coding and coanalytic transfinite recursion. The complexity is optimal: proper subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ of positive Hausdorff dimension and bases of the stated kinds cannot be analytic.
